title: Gemstones by planet: the full navaratna guide | Ask Tota
description: All nine planetary gemstones, the metals, days and fingers traditionally prescribed, the two schools that disagree about who should wear what, and how not to get robbed.
og_title: Gemstones by planet, and when not to wear one
og_description: Nine grahas, nine stones. Here is the full traditional system, the disagreement at the heart of it, and the consumer guide nobody selling you a stone will give you.
h1: gemstones by planet, and when not to wear one
dek: nine grahas, nine stones, and an industry built on top of them. here is the complete navaratna table, the two schools that flatly disagree about who should wear what, and the questions that keep u from being robbed.

faq.q: which gemstone is for which planet?
faq.a: ruby for the sun, pearl for the moon, red coral for mars, emerald for mercury, yellow sapphire for jupiter, diamond for venus, blue sapphire for saturn, hessonite for rahu and cat's eye for ketu. together they are the navaratna, the nine gems.

faq.q: how do i know which gemstone i should wear?
faq.a: there is no single answer, because two schools disagree. one says strengthen ur weakest graha. the other says never strengthen a graha that rules difficult houses for ur lagna, and only ever wear stones for ur lagna lord and ur yogakaraka. ask which school ur astrologer follows.

no. there is no measured mechanism by which a mineral affects a planet or a life outcome, and no replicated study showing an effect. the tradition is real and old. the causal claim is not established.

faq.q: which gemstones should never be worn together?
faq.a: traditional practice avoids pairing stones of grahas treated as enemies, most commonly blue sapphire with ruby or with red coral, and diamond with ruby or pearl. practitioners differ on the details.

the traditional indian weight unit for gemstones. one ratti is roughly 0.91 carat, or about 0.18 grams. prescriptions are usually given in ratti, while the market prices in carats, and the gap between the two is a common place to be overcharged.

faq.q: what are upratna or substitute stones?
faq.a: cheaper stones traditionally accepted in place of the main gem. red garnet for ruby, moonstone for pearl, carnelian for coral, peridot or green tourmaline for emerald, citrine or yellow topaz for yellow sapphire, white sapphire for diamond, amethyst or iolite for blue sapphire.

faq.q: why is blue sapphire considered risky?
faq.a: because it is saturn's stone and saturn is the graha of consequence, tradition treats it as the most reactive of the nine. that reputation is also why it is sold with a three day trial, a test framed so that any outcome confirms the seller's advice.

faq.q: which finger should i wear my gemstone on?
faq.a: commonly given as: ruby and yellow sapphire on the index or ring finger, pearl on the little finger, coral on the ring finger, emerald on the little finger, diamond on the middle or ring finger, blue sapphire, hessonite and cat's eye on the middle finger. practitioners vary.

faq.q: does the gemstone need to touch my skin?
faq.a: traditional practice says yes, the stone should be set so its underside touches the skin. that is a convention of the practice, not a physical requirement of anything.

faq.q: how do i avoid being sold a fake?
faq.a: buy the stone and the advice from different people, insist on a certificate from an independent laboratory, get the treatment status in writing, check price per carat against the open market, and never accept urgency.

faq.q: is a heated or treated sapphire acceptable?
faq.a: traditional practice generally prefers untreated natural stones, and treated ones cost far less. the important thing is that u are told which u are buying, in writing, before u pay.

faq.q: what should i do instead of buying a stone?
faq.a: if the goal is to feel less anxious about a chart, read the chart properly first. most gemstone purchases follow a frightening reading, and a clear reading removes the fear more reliably than a mineral does.
